title: MCP server registration is broken and has no working entrypoint
evidence: mcp_server.py:831-832 runs `mcp_server.tool()(tool)` at module import against `Server` from mcp.server (the low-level SDK Server); that class has no `.tool()` method — only `list_tools()`/`call_tool()`/`run()` decorators (confirmed in installed mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py:440,498,646), so the import raises AttributeError. `handle_tool` (mcp_server.py:770) is never wired via @call_tool, get_tools() is never wired via @list_tools, and there is no stdio entrypoint / mcp_server.run() / __main__. Tool definitions (get_tools, mcp_server.py:670) and a dispatch handler exist, but the server cannot run.
suggestion: Register with `@mcp_server.list_tools()` returning get_tools() and `@mcp_server.call_tool()` delegating to handle_tool, then add an async main using mcp.server.stdio.stdio_server() + mcp_server.run(); guard with `if __name__ == "__main__"`.

title: `mcp` dependency undeclared in requirements.txt
evidence: mcp_server.py:13-14 imports `from mcp.server import Server` and `from mcp.types import TextContent, ImageContent, Tool`, but requirements.txt lists only fastapi, uvicorn, pandas, python-dotenv, sse-starlette — no `mcp`. A clean `pip install -r requirements.txt` then `import mcp_server` fails with ModuleNotFoundError.
suggestion: Add `mcp` (the Model Context Protocol SDK) to requirements.txt with a pinned version.

title: test_get_player_by_name conditionally skips when FIFA data absent
evidence: test_soccer.py:123 `pytest.skip("FIFA data not available")` — runtime-conditional skip on player-search coverage.
suggestion: Ship a small FIFA fixture so player tests always execute, or assert the data is present.
